correctness.rationale: Putting u_n=-log x_n gives u_(n+1)=p u_n-log c+O(exp(-delta u_n)); summing the normalized affine recurrence gives u_n=C p^n+(log c)/(p-1)+o(1), C>0 from u_n->infinity. Algebraic flight durations satisfy tau_n~a exp(q C p^n), so t_n is dominated by the last term and log log t_n=n log p+O(1); logarithmic flights have tau_n~a C p^n, hence t_n~const p^n and log t_n=n log p+O(1). Bracketing T between consecutive returns gives matching N(T) asymptotics. Summing b_n by Cesàro and bounding incomplete-cycle outside-time gives L(T)~b0 N(T). The cited piecewise example gives r(x)=sqrt(1+x^2)-1, return r/(1+r-r²)=x²/2-3x^4/8+O(x^6), tau~2/x² and b0=1-2epsilon. Independent symbolic expansion and recurrence checks corroborated constants.

value.rationale: Physically motivated quantitative refinement of statistical attraction: the same superattracting return-map order yields different observable occupation decay depending on algebraic versus saddle-logarithmic flight times; gives universal leading coefficients for each.

final_claim: For a superattracting one-dimensional return x_(n+1)=c x_n^p(1+O(x_n^delta)), p>1, and outside-time b_n->b0>0, flight times asymptotic to a x_n^(-q) give L(T)~(b0/log p)log log T, whereas times asymptotic to a log(1/x_n) give L(T)~(b0/log p)log T; the original piecewise flow example has p=2 and b0=1-2epsilon.
limitations: Conditional positive scalar return law, specified flight-time classes and bounded partial-cycle outside time, not every statistical attractor.
No uniform error estimates or claims for parabolic p=1 dynamics.
